COREUniformityThe rule behind the rules.

CORE-01

Explicit rules take priority for new code. Follow the surrounding code only where no explicit rule applies. A new rule does not require rewriting existing code; that refactoring can happen separately.

docs/README.md

An explicit rule requires error: use function (error) in new code even beside older function (err) handlers.

CORE-02

Unwritten conventions bind too. An unwritten convention is still a convention. File names, CSS classes, formatting and even attribute order follow the same systematic approach — silence is not permission.

docs/README.md
CORE-03

An option is "value" and "label". A selectable option is always {value, label} — value is internal, label is displayed. Select, dropdown, radio, tabs alike.

value_label.md
{value: <internal>, label: <display>}
CORE-04

Opposites come from the established pairs, not from invention. req/res is Express-only; res/rej is valid for Promise executors, as are the full names resolve/reject.

docs/README.md
construct/destruct  create/destroy
open/close          begin/end
start/finish        first/last
next/previous       get/put
src/dest            source/destination
res/rej (Promise)   resolve/reject
req/res (Express)   request/response
setup/teardown      push/pull
enabled/disabled    import/export

NAMENaming grammarVerb morphology decides function or data.

NAME-01

Functions are verbs; data are nouns. Functions are verb phrases, data are noun phrases. Each assignment reads as a sentence — the verb performs, the noun holds.

docs/README.md
const users_by_role = users_group_by_role(users);
NAME-02

The verb form marks function or data. English verb morphology is the marker. An imperative verb makes a function; a past participle makes data. Where there is no verb, a function marker — _from_, _to_, _of_, check_ — makes a function. One exception: a linter rule's function is named after its rule id, as ESLint does, block_layout(context) for block-layout.

naming_markers.md
items_sort_by_time(items)   // function
items_sorted_by_time        // data
NAME-03

A bare "by" name is data, never called. A bare _by_ name is always data, never a function: it is read with brackets, or with .get() when it is a Map — never called.

naming_markers.md
user_by_id[id]       ✓ right
user_by_id.get(id)   ✓ right, a Map
user_by_id(id)       ✗ wrong
NAME-04

The first word's plural states what a key returns. Plurality of the first word states lookup cardinality — what one key returns, not how big the container is.

var_names.md
user_by_id[id]                    // User
users_by_role[role]               // User[]
children_by_parent_id[parent_id]  // Node[]
NAME-05

"Sorted by" is the same data, reordered. _sorted_by_ marks data of the same shape, reordered. The participle survives here because it carries what shape alone cannot.

naming_markers.md
items_sorted_by_time   // Item[], still an array
NAME-06

_per_ marks a ratio or a rate.

naming_markers.md
clicks_per_visit
NAME-07

Group by, sort by, index by produce them. The operations that produce those shapes are _group_by_, _sort_by_ and _index_by_. The criterion follows the verb.

naming_markers.md
users_index_by_id(users)     // user_by_id
users_group_by_role(users)   // users_by_role
items_sort_by_time(items)    // items_sorted_by_time
NAME-08

"From" means computed: result first, source last. Use _from_ only when something is computed, parsed or constructed — result first, source last.

naming_markers.md
user_from_token(token)
date_from_timestamp(ts)
tree_from_array(rows)
NAME-09

_from_ never means lookup. A lookup disguised as construction is wrong.

naming_markers.md

user_from_id(id)   ✗ wrong
user_by_id[id]     ✓ right
![an id looked up in the user_by_id table: user_by_id[id] is right, user_from_id(id) dresses the lookup as construction](../img/rules/from_is_not_lookup.svg)

NAME-10

"To" only in method position. _to_ is for method position only, where the source is the receiver.

naming_markers.md
tree.to_json()
NAME-11

No "to" in data names. _to_ is banned in data names — id_to_name is only a second spelling of name_by_id.

naming_markers.md
id_to_name    ✗ banned
name_by_id    ✓ right
NAME-12

No "indexed by"; bare "by" says it. _indexed_by_ does not exist. Bare _by_ already names that shape.

naming_markers.md
users_indexed_by_id   ✗ does not exist
user_by_id            ✓ right
NAME-13

"Grouped by" only for invariant plurals. _grouped_by_ is retired from data names except for invariant plurals — fish, data, series — which cannot state cardinality by plurality. Prefer a countable noun when one exists.

var_names.md
fish_by_tank           // Record<tank, Fish>
fish_grouped_by_tank   // Record<tank, Fish[]>
rows_by_source         ✓ over data_by_source
NAME-14

"Of" queries possession. _of_ is a possession query.

naming_markers.md
descendants_of(node)
NAME-15

"is" names a boolean, a predicate or data. is_ names a boolean: a predicate that returns one, or data that holds one. It is not a function marker; a check that must read as a call is check_*, a verb.

naming_markers.md
is_ancestor(a, b)   // a predicate, called
is_open             // a boolean, read
check_status()      // a check that reads as a call
NAME-16

A conversion and its variable share a first word. A standalone conversion and the variable it fills share their first word.

naming_markers.md
const json = json_from_tree(tree);
NAME-17

Names start with the domain. Naming is domain-first. Functions and files follow items_*, item_* or domain nouns; generic names are avoided.

FORMATTING.md
items_index_by_uid()   ✓ right
process() handle() util()   ✗ avoid
NAME-18

Verb-first families are the exceptions. The verb-first families are the exceptions to domain-first naming: main — reserved for the entry function of an executable script — format_*, render_*, export_*, is_*, refresh_*, click_*, emit_*, and the steps of a script (build_glossaries_html()). A step is a function main() calls once, in order, to do one part of the work; a verb-first name that is not a step is renamed when next touched.

FORMATTING.md
function main()
{
    report_print();
}

VARVariablesA name states the shape of its data.

VAR-01

A variable name states the shape of its data.

var_names.md
users                  // User[]
user_by_id             // Record<id, User>
users_by_role          // Record<role, User[]>
items_sorted_by_time   // Item[], reordered
VAR-02

Name the result out. A variable the function builds and returns unchanged is named out — return out;, exactly. A parameter, a loop variable or an outer value returned unchanged keeps its own name: return user;.

return_out.md
function emails_from_users(users)
{
    const out = [];
    for (const user of users) {
        if (user.email) {
            out.push(user.email);
        }
    }
    return out;
}
VAR-03

out never leaves the function. The caller names the result by what it means.

return_out.md
const emails = emails_from_users(users);
const users_by_role = users_group_by_role(users);
VAR-04

Return a literal directly. Returning a literal or an expression directly is allowed; a guard return may return null, false, [], {}. const out = {...}; return out; is rewritten as return {...};

FORMATTING.md
const out = {a, b};
return out;          ✗ rewrite this

return {a, b};       ✓ as this
VAR-05

Errors use e in arrows, error in regular handlers. A caught error is error in a catch binding or regular function, and e in an arrow. This applies to promise rejection handlers and EventEmitter error listeners. Callback names stay e / error at every depth. DOM error events follow VAR-16; only nested catch bindings use numbered names (VAR-17).

var_names_error.md
promise.catch(e => report(e));

server.on('error', function (error) {
    throw error;
});

catch (error) {
    console.log(error.message);
}
VAR-06

Reserve e for error arrows; no err or ex. e names an arrow error parameter. A regular error parameter or catch binding uses error, never e, err or ex; only catch bindings get the nested numbers in VAR-17.

var_names_error.md
catch (e)     ✗ no
catch (err)   ✗ no
catch (error) ✓ yes

promise.catch(e => report(e));   ✓ yes
VAR-07

Name stderr text by what it is. Accumulated stderr text is not an error variable. Name it by what it is.

var_names_error.md
stderr   ✓ right
err      ✗ wrong
VAR-08

Prefer explicit temporaries. Use intermediate variables instead of nested expressions; favor clarity over terseness.

FORMATTING.md
VAR-09

Arrow values use v; arrow errors use e. A lone value or event parameter is v; nested value arrows use vv, then vvv, by total arrow depth, including error arrows. Error arrows keep e at every depth (VAR-05). With several parameters, choose names for their roles; an error callback’s first parameter still follows the error naming rule.

FORMATTING.md
items.map(v => v.uid)
items.some(v => v.sizes.some(vv => vv.width > 100))
promise.catch(e => report(e))
VAR-10

The for...of loop variable is the singular of the collection.

for_of.md
for (const user of users) { }
for (const child of node.children) { }
VAR-11

A cached length is "end". A cached array length in a single loop is named end.

for_i_end_ii_jj_kk.md
for (let i = 0, end = items.length; i < end; ++i) {
}
VAR-12

Nested bounds double the index: ii, jj, kk. In nested loops the cached bound is the doubled index name: i → ii, j → jj, k → kk.

for_i_end_ii_jj_kk.md
for (let i = 0, ii = foo.length; i < ii; ++i) {
    for (let j = 0, jj = bar.length; j < jj; ++j) {
        for (let k = 0, kk = baz.length; k < kk; ++k) {
        }
    }
}
VAR-13

A transformed or conditional result is not "out". Only that variable is out. A value that is joined, stringified or otherwise transformed on its way out, or returned only on a condition (?:, if), is not out; it is named by what it is.

return_out.md
VAR-14

Start time is "time0". The variable holding the start time of a measurement is always named time0. The elapsed time is the current time minus time0: a number, shown to a person only through format_duration (FN-02), never as ${Date.now() - time0}ms at the call site.

var_names_time0.md
$time0 = microtime(true);
echo format_duration(microtime(true) - $time0);

const time0 = Date.now();
console.log(format_duration(Date.now() - time0));
VAR-15

Use time0 for measurement; paired names for other roles. Do not name an elapsed-time start begin, start or t0. Outside that role, use start/finish or begin/end when the pair is actually used.

var_names_time0.md
const time0 = Date.now();  // elapsed-time measurement

const start = range.start;
const finish = range.finish;
VAR-16

Events use v in arrows, event in regular functions. A DOM event is a value, including an event whose type is error. A one-parameter arrow uses v; a regular event handler uses event. Reserve e for error values in arrows.

var_names_event.md
el.addEventListener('click', v => v.stopPropagation());
el.addEventListener('error', v => report(v));

el.addEventListener('error', function (event) {
    report(event);
});
VAR-17

Nested catch bindings use error2, error3. A catch inside another catch names its binding error2, the next level error3. This applies only to catch bindings: callback parameters stay e in arrows and error in regular functions, even inside a catch.

var_names_event.md
catch (error) {
    try {
        await save_backup(scene);
    }
    catch (error2) {
    }
}
VAR-18

A generic name has one meaning. i, j, k, end, ii, v, e, error, event, out, time0, req and res each mean one thing, listed on one page; anywhere else the variable is named by what it holds.

generic_names.md
const out = [...new Set(tags)];
return (out.length === tags.length) ? tags : out;   ✗ no

const unique_tags = [...new Set(tags)];
return (unique_tags.length === tags.length) ? tags : unique_tags;   ✓ yes
VAR-19

A configuration value at the top is UPPER_CASE. A constant the module keeps as configuration, a global name for a value set in the code, is written in upper case at the module's top level. A const inside a function or a block is lower case. Imports are not this rule.

MANUALLY_APPROVED_RULES.md
const PRESS_MS = 400;           // the module's top

function press_start(event)
{
    const started = Date.now();  // inside
}

FNFunction contractsWhat a prefix promises the caller.

FN-01

"format" strictly returns human-facing text. format_* returns a string to show to a person, including when the value comes from object state.

format_xxx.md
format_bytes(1457664)    // "1.4 MB"
format_duration(155000)  // "2m 35s"
format_usd(1299)         // "$12.99"
FN-05

"render" constructs asset content. render_* constructs content such as CSS, HTML or SVG from state. The result can be a string; its purpose is an asset rather than a human-facing formatted value.

render_xxx.md
public function render_css(): string
{
    return "body { color: {$this->text_color}; }";
}
FN-02

Never hand-roll a display conversion. A display conversion is never hand-rolled at a call site — an inline one is a missed format_*.

format_xxx.md
${Math.round(bytes / 1024)}kB   ✗ missed call
format_bytes(bytes)             ✓ right
FN-03

format_* returns — it never prints. Output is the caller’s job.

format_xxx.md
console.log(format_tree(tree));
FN-04

"format" is not serialization. format_* is not for machine formats. Serialization is conversion, not display.

format_xxx.md
format_user(user)     // "Alex K. (admin)" — humans
json_from_user(user)  // machines
FN-06

"render" is recomputed, never stored. The prefix separates constructed content from stored attributes. render_* is recomputed per call — never cached, never stored.

render_xxx.md
$this->text_color     // stored attribute
$this->render_css()   // constructed content
FN-07

"render" may return null or throw. render_* may return null when not applicable, and may throw when the state makes the value meaningless.

render_xxx.md
if (!$this->theme) {
    return null;
}
FN-08

"render" is sync and pure; downloads are "export". render_* constructs content without DOM updates, file writes or downloads, and always returns its result. A function that brings a part of the page up to date returns nothing and is refresh_<what> (FN-10), never <what>_render. A downloadable artifact — zip, csv or xlsx — is export_*, which may be async and side-effectful.

render_xxx.md
$theme->render_css()    // construct CSS content
refresh_theme_labels()  // bring a part of the page up to date
export_zip()            // produce a downloadable artifact
FN-09

Format and render differ by output purpose. format_* returns a string a person reads; render_* constructs asset content. Both may return strings; reading object state does not turn display text into render output.

format_xxx.md
format_bytes(1457664)   // "1.4 MB", human-facing text
$theme->render_css()   // CSS asset content
FN-10

A local copy of remote data has "refresh". Anything that holds a local copy of remote data has refresh() — it pulls the data and brings the local vars up to date. Mental model: the browser refresh button.

refresh.md
refresh: async function () {
    await Promise.all([
        this.refresh_user(),
        this.refresh_photos(),
    ]);
},
FN-11

Refresh is safe to call anytime. refresh() is idempotent — safe to call at any moment, any number of times.

refresh.md
FN-12

Refresh composes per-part refreshes. A fine-grained refresh_<part>() syncs one part of the state; refresh() composes them.

refresh.md
refresh_user: async function () {
    this.user = await fetch_user();
},
FN-13

Init is the first refresh.

refresh.md
mounted: async function () {
    await this.refresh();
    this.ready = true;
},
FN-14

A modal returns a commit flag. An interaction — modal, popover — executes its own logic and returns a boolean commit flag. It expresses intent; it does not expose control flow. These are the best practices for vue-modal: modal.return(true) inside, await modal_x().promise() at the call site.

interactions-should-return-only-boolean-flag.md
// true  → changes were committed
// false → no-op (cancel, or no changes)
if (await modal_upload().promise()) {
    await blocking(this.refresh());
}
FN-15

Guards return early. Validate inputs immediately and return null or empty values explicitly.

FORMATTING.md
FN-16

One public value per library module. A reusable module exports one function, class, configuration or data value. Executable scripts export nothing; tool-shaped files follow the tool.

FORMATTING.md

FMTFormattingBraces, breaks, blank lines, comments.

FMT-01

Four spaces, no tabs. Indentation is exactly 4 spaces. No tabs.

FORMATTING.md
FMT-02

A top-level function declaration puts its opening brace on the next line.

FORMATTING.md
function main()
{
}
FMT-03

Nested function: brace on the same line. A function declared inside another function keeps its opening brace on the declaration line.

FORMATTING.md
function main()
{
    function limit_print(limit) {
    }
}
FMT-04

Callbacks keep the brace on the line. Function expressions, callbacks and Promise executors keep the opening brace on the declaration line.

formatting_blocks.md
server.on('error', function (error) {
    // ...
});

return new Promise(function (resolve, reject) {
    // ...
});
FMT-05

Class brace below; method brace inline. A class declaration puts its brace on the next line; its methods keep the brace on the declaration line.

formatting_blocks.md
class Logger
{
    constructor(parent_group_uid) {
    }

    write(format, ...values) {
    }
}
FMT-07

Always use braces. Always use braces for if, else, for, while. No single-line bodies.

FORMATTING.md
if (!user) return null;   ✗ no

if (!user) {              ✓ yes
    return null;
}
FMT-08

else starts on a new line.

FORMATTING.md
if (a) {
}
else if (b) {
}
else {
}
FMT-09

catch and finally start on a new line.

formatting_blocks.md
try {
}
catch (error) {
}
finally {
}
FMT-10

Align "switch" and "case". switch and case are aligned at the same indentation level.

FORMATTING.md
switch (type) {
case 'voice':
    break;
case 'text':
    break;
default:
}
FMT-11

Keep short objects on one line; expand only when needed. Multiple fields alone do not require line breaks. When size or nested structure requires a multi-line object literal, use one field per line and a trailing comma.

formatting_blocks.md
const next = {uid: item.uid, parent_uid: item.parent_uid, index};
FMT-12

Options-style methods are always function expressions. Even a return-only method without its own this or arguments keeps that form; the tiny-arrow rule applies to callbacks and value factories.

formatting_blocks.md
const options = {
    refresh: async function () {
    },
    px: function (value) {
        return value ? `${value}px` : '0';
    },
};
FMT-13

Keep an expression on one line when it fits on one line.

FORMATTING.md
FMT-14

Never break after "=" before a call. Never split an assignment after = when its right-hand side is a single function call.

FORMATTING.md
const users_by_role =
    users_group_by_role(users);   ✗ no

const users_by_role = users_group_by_role(users);   ✓ yes
FMT-15

Break lines only to show structure. Break a statement only when its size or nested structure makes the break necessary. Line breaks must expose structure.

FORMATTING.md
FMT-16

A blank line marks a phase change — nothing else. Add one only when the following statement begins an independent conceptual step.

FORMATTING.md
FMT-17

Keep setup next to its use. Keep setup adjacent to the loop, condition or call that immediately uses it. Tightly coupled setup and use are not separated merely because the statement type changes.

FORMATTING.md
FMT-18

Build objects from needed fields only. Construct an object from the required fields only. Do not spread a full object when a subset is needed.

FORMATTING.md
{...item, index}                              ✗ bad
{uid: item.uid, parent_uid: item.parent_uid, index}   ✓ good
FMT-19

Comment intent, not mechanics. Comments explain intent or policy only. No comments for obvious mechanics.

FORMATTING.md
FMT-20

Multi-line comments carry rules or guarantees. A multi-line comment carries a rule, an invariant or a guarantee.

FORMATTING.md
FMT-21

Every route has a route comment. Every route function carries a route comment directly above it: METHOD /path (params).

endpoint_comment.md
// Express route handler
// GET /file/<name>
async function file_get(req, res)
{
}
FMT-22

Parentheses only when the route takes input. Parentheses appear only when the endpoint takes input — body, headers, query, comma-separated, in that order.

endpoint_comment.md
// Express route handler
// POST /upload (body, header:x-filename)
function upload_post(req, res)
{
}
FMT-23

Headers prefixed; path params in the path. A header is prefixed with header:; a path parameter is spelled in the path itself.

endpoint_comment.md
header:x-filename
/file/<name>
FMT-24

An intent comment continues the same block on the next line.

endpoint_comment.md
// POST /upload (body, header:x-filename)
// Streams to data/ before the body is fully read.
FMT-25

Named functions outside class bodies are "function" declarations. Every named function outside a class — top-level or nested — is a function name(...) declaration. Class methods use their class syntax.

FORMATTING.md
function report_print()
{
}
FMT-26

No spaces inside one-line braces. A single-line object or array literal has no space inside its braces or brackets — a standalone literal, a nested one, or one row of a list.

FORMATTING.md
{ value: 'today', label: 'Today' }   ✗ no
{value: 'today', label: 'Today'}     ✓ yes

[ 'remote', 'host', 'service' ]     ✗ no
['remote', 'host', 'service']       ✓ yes
FMT-27

Parenthesize compound operands in logic. In a logical expression (&&, ||, ??) and in the condition of a ternary, an operand that carries an operator of its own is wrapped in parentheses. A simple operand — identifier, member access, call, template literal, unary negation — stays bare, and a chain of one logical operator is one expression.

FORMATTING.md
return is_dev || i === end - 1;     ✗ no
return is_dev || (i === end - 1);   ✓ yes

(state === 'done') ? 'ok' : 'wait'
FMT-28

One variable per declaration. Each variable gets its own const or let statement; a declaration never lists several variables separated by commas. The header of an indexed loop is the exception.

FORMATTING.md
const osc = c.createOscillator(),
    gain = c.createGain();          ✗ no

const osc = c.createOscillator();
const gain = c.createGain();        ✓ yes
FMT-29

One blank line between top-level functions. Top-level functions stand one blank line apart: each function declared at module level is followed by one blank line before the next one.

FORMATTING.md
}
function toggle_sound()   ✗ no blank line

}

function toggle_sound()   ✓ one blank line
FMT-30

Only the last argument spans lines. Only the last argument of a call may span several lines; nothing follows a multi-line argument — no further argument after }, no chained call after }). A function that would leave arguments dangling is declared inside the caller and passed by name; a chained call becomes a variable.

FORMATTING.md
page.evaluate(function (text) {
    // ...
}, text);                          ✗ dangling

page.evaluate(find_families, text);   ✓ yes

items.filter(function (item) {
    // ...
}).map(v => v.uid);               ✗ dangling
FMT-31

Build strings with template literals. A string built from parts is a template literal; + never joins a string to a value. Plain quotes stay for a string with nothing to interpolate.

FORMATTING.md
'weapons/turret-' + weapon.id    ✗ no
`weapons/turret-${weapon.id}`    ✓ yes
FMT-32

An empty function is {} on one line. An empty function expression or arrow is a no-op, as ignore is: its body is {} on one line, never split over two. A function declaration and a method keep their braces on lines of their own; a body holding only a comment is not empty.

FORMATTING.md
params.update = params.update || function () {
};                                                ✗ no

params.update = params.update || function () {};   ✓ yes
promise.catch(() => {});                          ✓ yes

FLOWControl flowImperative, explicit, no magic.

FLOW-01

Prefer imperative control flow.

FORMATTING.md
FLOW-02

No index needed: use for...of. Prefer for...of when the index is not needed.

for_of.md
for (const item of items) {
}
FLOW-03

Use an indexed loop when the index is needed.

for_of.md
for (let i = 0, end = items.length; i < end; ++i) {
}
FLOW-04

No do...while. do { ... } while (...) does not exist. Use while or for.

FORMATTING.md
FLOW-05

Reduce and chains only on one line. reduce, deep chaining and functional pipelines are allowed only if the entire expression fits on a single line.

FORMATTING.md
FLOW-06

Arrows only for tiny callbacks. Do not use arrow functions for non-trivial logic. Arrows are allowed only for tiny callbacks.

FORMATTING.md
const uids = items.map(v => v.uid);
fresh.catch(ignore);
FLOW-07

A block-body arrow becomes a function. An arrow with a block body does not exist — it becomes function (...) {}, with an optional _this inside. The empty () => {}, a no-op, is the one exception (FMT-32).

formatting_blocks.md
request.on('end', async () => {          ✗ does not exist
});

request.on('end', async function () {     ✓ this
});
FLOW-08

A catch that ignores the error binds nothing.

formatting_blocks.md
try {
}
catch {
}
FLOW-09

Plain data: Set, Map or {}. Use plain data structures — Set, Map or plain {} for lookups. No prototypes, no mutation via shared state. A module may own its state, a singleton over its own data, written only by its own functions; shared means across modules, and that is what is forbidden.

FORMATTING.md
let modal = null;    // the module's own

function modal_show()
{
    modal = modal_make();
}
FLOW-10

No implicit magic or hidden side effects. No implicit magic. No hidden side effects, no reliance on execution-order side effects. The one visible exception: side-effect imports, which sit at the very top of the file, in the order they run (FILE-11).

FORMATTING.md
import './sass/main.sass';   // the top of the file, in run order
import './main-pre';

import Vue from 'vue';
FLOW-11

A return-only callback is an arrow. Options-style methods retain function expressions (FMT-12). A callback whose body is only return <expression>, and whose arrow fits on one line, is written as that arrow — the mirror of FLOW-07. function stays for a callback that does more, or that needs this or arguments.

FORMATTING.md
items.filter(function (item) {
    return item_text(item) === text;
});                                       ✗ no

items.filter(v => item_text(v) === text);   ✓ yes
FLOW-12

Names are written whole. A constant, function, method, class or property is never glued together from strings at run time; a search or a rename must find it. A value that picks one of a few known names lists them with match (PHP) or switch (JavaScript). A name built at run time only for an open set that cannot be listed.

names_written_whole.md
constant(Invoice::class.'::STATUS_'.strtoupper($status))   ✗ no

match ($status) {                                          ✓ yes
    'paid' => Invoice::STATUS_PAID,
    'void' => Invoice::STATUS_VOID,
}

FILEFile and module structureOne entry function, one fixed order.

FILE-01

A library module exports one public value last. The value may be a function, class, configuration or data. Declare it above and export its name at file end; tool-shaped files follow their tool.

FORMATTING.md
module.exports = items_index_by_uid;
FILE-02

A script runs main and exports nothing. An executable script uses main as its entry function and does not export.

FORMATTING.md
FILE-03

Library or executable, never both. Do not combine a library export and an executable invocation in the same file.

FORMATTING.md
FILE-04

An executable hands main to cli. An executable hands its entry function to cli. cli owns the process contract: it keeps the event loop alive until main settles, reports a failure, and exits non-zero — ExitCodeError picks the code, any other error exits 1.

cli_main.md
const cli = require('@vbarbarosh/node-helpers/src/cli');

cli(main);

async function main()
{
}
FILE-05

cli(main), never cli(main()). cli runs the function through Promise.try, so a synchronous throw is reported like a rejection; an already-invoked main() is a promise, and Promise.try rejects it with “expecting a function” — the app dies at startup.

cli_main.md
cli(main);     ✓ right
cli(main());   ✗ dies at startup
FILE-06

No hand-rolled catch and exit. A hand-rolled main().catch(...) with process.exit(1) does not exist.

cli_main.md
main().catch(function (error) {
    console.error(error);
    process.exit(1);
});                              ✗ does not exist
FILE-07

Nothing precedes the shebang. An executable script may start with a shebang; nothing may precede it.

FORMATTING.md
#!/usr/bin/env node
FILE-08

Imports sorted in byte order. The import block is sorted as plain text lines in byte order — what vim’s :sort over the block, or LC_ALL=C sort, produces. require and import alike.

FORMATTING.md
const $ = require('jquery');
const Vue = require('vue');
const axios = require('axios');
const cli = require('@vbarbarosh/node-helpers/src/cli');
const fs = require('fs');
const {promisify} = require('util');
FILE-09

The whole line is the sort key. The whole line is the sort key — const or import included, not the module path and not the variable name.

imports_sorted.md
FILE-10

Byte order, not locale order. Byte order, not locale order: @ and $ come before letters, uppercase before lowercase, and { after z — destructured imports land last.

imports_sorted.md
const Vue = require('vue');       ← V before a
const axios = require('axios');
const {promisify} = require('util'); ← { after z
FILE-11

Imports form one unbroken list. The import block is one contiguous list: no groups for builtins, packages and local files, and no blank lines or comments inside it — either one breaks the sort. Two exceptions: a side-effect import keeps its run order in its own block at the top, and the named imports ({foo, bar}) may stand apart after the default ones — one blank line between blocks.

imports_sorted.md
import './sass/main.sass';
import './main-pre';

import Vue from 'vue';
import axios from 'axios';

import {mapState} from 'vuex';
import {promisify} from 'util';
FILE-12

Constants follow the requires. File-level constants and variables follow the require statements.

FORMATTING.md
const report_limit = 31;
FILE-13

cli(main) right after initialization. cli(main); comes immediately after all global initialization, and no executable code other than that call may appear before the public entry function.

FORMATTING.md
FILE-14

The public entry function is the first function in the file. In an executable, the first function declaration is function main().

FORMATTING.md
FILE-15

Helpers follow the entry function. Helpers are defined after the public entry function, and before a library’s final export.

FORMATTING.md
FILE-16

Helpers must be named functions, not inline lambdas.

FORMATTING.md
FILE-17

This repository is CommonJS. This repository's own code and node scripts are CommonJS: const <name> = require('<module>');, never import or export. Elsewhere the rules cover both module systems.

FORMATTING.md
FILE-18

Libraries follow a fixed order. Library order is fixed.

FORMATTING.md
requires → constants → public entry → helpers → module.exports
FILE-19

Executables follow a fixed order. Executable order is fixed.

FORMATTING.md
shebang → requires → globals → cli(main); → main() → helpers
FILE-20

One library export, last, and the file bears its name. A reusable/library module exports one public value; the file is named after that value. Declare it above and export its name last: module.exports = name; or export default name;. Never combine an ES-module declaration with its export or export an inline expression. Executable scripts export nothing; tool-shaped files follow the tool.

one_export_per_file.md
// helper.js
function helper()
{
    return null;
}

export default helper;
FILE-21

No named exports; one public value per library module. Several independent public functions are several modules, each named after its export. One exported class can contain methods. Several names are never taken from a local module.

one_export_per_file.md
export {engine_run, engine_transport};                   ✗ no
import {engine_run, engine_transport} from './engine';   ✗ no

import engine_run from './engine_run';                   ✓ yes
import engine_transport from './engine_transport';
FILE-23

Reusable scratch and test modules export one value too. Research, scratch and test-support modules are not exempt. Executable scripts export nothing; tool-shaped files follow the tool.

one_export_per_file.md
FILE-24

Libraries and tools dictate their own shape. A named import from a library is the library’s shape, and a file whose shape is dictated by a tool follows the tool — module.exports.mochaHooks in a mocha hooks file.

one_export_per_file.md
import {mapState} from 'vuex';
FILE-25

New code takes its place from its surroundings where no explicit rule applies. Read the code around the insertion point — what stands together, in what order — and continue it within that scope. Explicit rules take priority (CORE-01); this does not require reorganizing existing code.

new_code_placement.md
FILE-26

A function family stays unbroken. A run of functions of one family — render_*, format_*, click_* — stays unbroken. A new member joins the run; a function of another family goes outside it, never between two members.

new_code_placement.md
render_css()
describe()            ✗ splits the run
render_html()

render_css()
render_html()
describe()            ✓ after the run

PROJProject layoutA directory is a program; bin/ holds its verbs.

PROJ-01

One project shape; bin/ holds the verbs. Every project keeps one shape. A directory is a program, and bin/ holds its methods — one executable per verb, working the same in every language.

layout.md
bin/build      bb
bin/configure
bin/release
bin/run        rr
bin/self-check
bin/test       tt
bin/watch      ww
PROJ-02

After git pull, run bin/configure. bin/configure is the only command to run after git pull to make a checkout ready for development.

layout.md
PROJ-03

Run, test, build and watch wrap npm. In a node.js project run, test, build and watch are thin wrappers over npm. The wrappers still earn their keep: rr, tt, bb, ww are shorter than any npm form, and the names hold for projects that are not node.js.

layout.md
alias rr='bin/run'
alias tt='bin/test'
alias bb='bin/build'
alias ww='bin/watch'
PROJ-04

build/ is never committed; dist/ is the release. bin/build puts what it builds into build/. build/ is temporary: it and everything in it are never committed. Taking something out of it into the repository is a decision of its own, as bin/release does with dist/. dist/ holds the released build, committed by bin/release at release time only. There is one build: bin/release runs it and copies build/ into dist/.

layout.md
build/   bin/build output, temporary, never committed
dist/    released build, committed by bin/release
PROJ-05

Runtime state in data/, never committed. data/ holds runtime state. Never committed.

layout.md
data/logs/2026-08-24.txt
PROJ-06

.env belongs to whoever runs the app. .env is not the application's: docker loads it, or the Dockerfile sets the variables. The rules set nothing for it.

layout.md
PROJ-07

config/ turns the environment into configuration. config/ is the one place of the application's configuration. config/index.js reads the environment variables, may load files, and gives the code its configuration ready to use, through one path.

layout.md
// config/index.js
module.exports = make_config(process.env);

const config = require('../config');
PROJ-08

src/ has a folder per part. src/ holds one subdirectory per part of the program.

layout.md
src/agent/    src/http/
src/android/  src/parser/
src/desktop-electron/
PROJ-09

Shared helpers go to src/helpers/. Small shared functions go to src/helpers/, one function per file.

layout.md
src/helpers/array_group.js
PROJ-10

A unit test sits next to the file it tests.

layout.md
src/helpers/array_group.js
src/helpers/array_group.test.js
PROJ-11

tests/ drives the whole program. tests/ holds suites that drive the whole program, such as playwright.

layout.md
PROJ-12

Keep the README short. README.md stays short: what the project is and how to start it.

layout.md
PROJ-13

Docs in docs/, notes in notes/, images in img/. docs/ holds the official documentation, notes/ holds working notes — hints and findings made during development — and img/ holds static images, mostly for the README.

layout.md
PROJ-14

The project root carries the same standard files.

layout.md
.env  .env.example  .gitignore  Dockerfile
LICENSE  README.md  package.json
PROJ-15

A script starts from bin/templ. A new bash script is a copy of bin/templ with what it does not need thrown away. Its header, strict mode included, and the script / scriptdir / scriptname lines always stay; the colors, the exit message, the temporary directory with its EXIT trap and the four echo lines stay only if the script uses them.

templ
#!/bin/bash

# http://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#The-Set-Builtin
# http://redsymbol.net/articles/unofficial-bash-strict-mode
set -o nounset -o errexit -o pipefail

script=`realpath $0`
scriptdir=`dirname $script`
scriptname=`basename $script`
PROJ-16

bin/configure asks everything up front. bin/configure asks every question it may have — the sudo password, a choice, a key — at the very start, before any work. Once the work has started there are no more questions; it never stops halfway, waiting for a password.

configure.md
PROJ-17

bin/configure takes sudo once, up front. bin/configure first works out what the run will need, predicting the state after the install. When a step will need sudo — an Electron chrome-sandbox that is missing, not root:4755, or about to be replaced by the install — it takes sudo -v up front, and the later calls are sudo -n, which fail at once rather than prompt.

configure.md
sandbox=node_modules/electron/dist/chrome-sandbox
state=`stat -c %U:%a $sandbox 2>/dev/null`
wanted=…      # electron in package-lock.json
installed=…   # electron in node_modules
if [ "$wanted" != "$installed" ] || [ "$state" != "root:4755" ]; then
    sudo -v
fi

sudo -n chown root:root $sandbox   # later: never a prompt
PROJ-18

Everything kept lives in data/. data/ is the project's permanent data: a restart, a redeploy or a migration does not delete it. Everything the program writes and has to keep lives under data/, and nowhere else. Configuration is not there: it comes from config/ and the environment.

data.md
PROJ-19

Docker images carry code, not data. A docker image carries the code, never the data. One mount of data/ — a named volume or a host directory — is all it takes to keep it; moving the project is moving its data/ and running it with the same environment.

data.md
docker run -v app-data:/app/data app
docker run -v /srv/app/data:/app/data app
PROJ-20

The README runs in a fixed order. A GitHub README.md runs in one order: badges, cover image, name, short description, website, quick start, documentation, license. Badges, the website link and the further documentation pages may be absent; the rest are always there.

readme.md
PROJ-21

Badges at the top, a row per kind. Badges sit at the very top, above the cover, a row per kind: the package and its numbers on one row, the CI workflows on the next. As many as the project has.

readme.md
PROJ-22

The cover image lives in img/. The cover image is a file in img/, shown with <picture> and a dark twin when the colours need one.

readme.md
<picture>
  <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="img/cover-dark.png">
  <img alt="rules" src="img/cover.png">
</picture>
PROJ-23

The repository name is the one heading. The name is the one # heading, right under the cover: the name of the repository.

readme.md
# rules
PROJ-24

One description sentence everywhere. The short description is one sentence on its own line, and the same sentence is the repository's About text and the description of package.json.

readme.md
PROJ-25

A link with the text Website follows the description. Its address is the repository's About → Website and the homepage of package.json. It is left out when the website is the documentation.

readme.md
**[Website](https://vbarbarosh.github.io/rules/)**
PROJ-26

A quick start in a few lines. A quick start shows how to install and run the project, in a few lines.

readme.md
npx vbarbarosh/rules src
PROJ-27

Documentation opens with the full docs link. A ## Documentation section opens with the link to the full documentation. Further pages follow as a short list, each with what it covers.

readme.md
## Documentation

Full documentation: **[docs/rules.html](docs/rules.html)**

* [Formatting](FORMATTING.md) — the JavaScript spec
PROJ-28

License is the last section. ## License is the last section: the license named and linked to LICENSE.

readme.md
## License

[MIT](LICENSE)
PROJ-29

Demos live in demos/. Small demos — a short runnable file that shows how something is used — live in demos/, never in examples/.

layout.md
demos/items_by.js      ✓ right
examples/items_by.js   ✗ wrong
PROJ-30

The build ends with the self-check. The last step of bin/build runs bin/self-check: the application's own check that it is fit to work, one probe per thing it needs, the programs it calls and what the build was to produce; a lit lamp names what to fix (TEST-09). A build that fails it ships nothing.

layout.md
# bin/build, the last step
bin/self-check

[ffmpeg] ffmpeg version 6.1.1
[pyftsubset] zopfli: 4120 < 5312 bytes
build/front.d: missing      ✗ ships nothing

RELPackaging and releaseShip a prebuilt dist/.

REL-01

Ship a prebuilt dist/. Distribute a prebuilt dist/ from the repository, the way Vue, VueRouter, Vuex, jQuery, Bootstrap, Axios, Cuid and Jsondiffpatch do.

packaging.md
<script src="https://unpkg.com/vue@2.6.11/dist/vue.js"></script>
REL-02

Release order: clean, bump, build, commit, tag. The release workflow is fixed: ensure there are no changes, increase the version, update dist/, commit, tag. dist/ is updated by the one build, then a copy of build/ (MP-32).

packaging.md
rm -rf build
npm run build
rm -rf dist
cp -r build dist
git add package.json package-lock.json dist
git commit -m "release: v$(...)"
git tag v$(...)
REL-03

The script commits and tags, not the bump. Bump the version without committing or tagging, then own both steps in the script.

packaging.md
npm version $1 --no-git-tag-version
REL-04

One command does the whole release. bin/release major|minor|patch performs the whole release.

packaging.md
bin/release patch
REL-05

A release script runs under bash strict mode.

packaging.md
set -o nounset -o errexit -o pipefail
REL-06

A bad argument prints usage to stderr and exits 1.

packaging.md
echo usage: release 'major|minor|patch' >&2
exit 1

GITCommitsA lowercase title, scope first; details below; 72 characters a line.

GIT-01

A commit title is a scope, a colon and a short description. The scope is one or two words: the part of the project the commit changes, its category.

commits.md
maps: placement rules for gates and portals, and map-check
GIT-02

Commit titles are lowercase. The title is all lowercase, names included.

commits.md
readme: elites and arcade saves as the code has them   ✓ yes
README: Elites and arcade saves                        ✗ no
GIT-03

A commit title is 72 characters at most. The whole title, scope included, stays within 72 characters. Short is the rule; 72 is the ceiling, not a target.

commits.md
maps: one name for the gate jump reach     38
docs: build-docs and a github pages workflow     44
72 at most
GIT-04

A short body, only when needed. Details go in a body after one blank line, only when they are really needed. A body is short, in ordinary sentences.

commits.md
docs: link the placement rules, gates and portals as they stand

docs/README.md lists placement.md; objects.md describes gates and
portals as the placement rules now put them.
GIT-05

A body wraps at 72 characters. Every line of the body stays within 72 characters, as the title does, and breaks between words. A path, a URL or a command longer than that keeps a line of its own, whole.

commits.md
docs: the agents page has a picture for each guide

Consequences first: the task, its four what-if questions and what each
shapes. One example, all cases: only the shown dropdown fixed against
every case found.

LOGLogsOne line, one event, four fields.

LOG-01

One line, one event, four fields. A log is one infinite file. One physical line records one event, in four fields and nothing else.

logs.md
[time][group_uid][sender] details
LOG-02

Measurements go in details. Elapsed time, status and every other measurement belong in details, not in a field of their own.

logs.md
[cd8e5vqp][db_query_end_error] 30.001s ETIMEDOUT
LOG-03

time is ISO-8601 UTC with milliseconds.

logs.md
2026-08-17T16:09:20.185Z
LOG-04

Omit time when the runtime stamps it. Include time when writing directly to a file; omit it when the runtime already timestamps the line, as docker does.

logs.md
[2026-08-17T16:09:20.185Z][cd8e5vqp][db_query_begin] name=select_users
[cd8e5vqp][db_query_begin] name=select_users
LOG-05

Every event carries its group uid. A group is one unit of work — a request, a job, a cron run. Every event carries its group’s uid, an opaque string, usually a cuid.

logs.md
LOG-06

A group opens with group_spawn. The first event of a group is group_spawn, emitted synchronously before the uid is passed to other work or another event is emitted for the group. A root group omits parent=.

logs.md
[new_group_uid][group_spawn] parent=old_group_uid
[c1a0root][group_spawn]
LOG-07

The caller's uid becomes the parent. Messages and requests carry the caller’s uid; the receiver uses it as the parent of its new group.

logs.md
LOG-08

A sender names one call site. sender identifies one logging call site, and the name is unique in the whole codebase — a grep for it lands on one place. Think of it as a const in a single namespace.

logs.md
LOG-09

sender is snake_case.

logs.md
^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$
LOG-10

Every begin is closed by its end. A _begin event is closed by the same stem with _end_ok or _end_error, in the same group. An end never appears without its begin in that group.

logs.md
[c9k2vf3p][mp4gif_worker_begin]
[c9k2vf3p][mp4gif_worker_end_ok] 4.512s

[c7t0xb1m][mp4gif_worker_begin]
[c7t0xb1m][mp4gif_worker_end_error] 0.884s ffmpeg exit=1
LOG-11

A plain end when the outcome speaks. Use _end when the logged outcome — an HTTP status, say — already says what happened and classifying it as ok or error would mislead.

logs.md
LOG-12

Spawn a group only when it pays. A group costs at least three lines. Spawn one only when the work earns them: seconds of work, or many logging call sites. Do not spawn a group for one short call.

logs.md
[bbb][group_spawn] parent=aaa
[bbb][process_begin]
[bbb][process_end_ok] 0.000s      ✗ noise
LOG-13

Log short work on the caller’s group, not a new one. When nothing is reported between the two ends, record one event.

logs.md
[aaa][process_begin]
[aaa][process_end_ok] 0.000s

[aaa][process_handled] 0.000s     ✓ even better
LOG-14

No lone end in a new group. Two lines are the same noise when a new group holds a lone end. The matching begin was emitted on the parent — keep the pair there.

logs.md
[bbb][group_spawn] parent=aaa
[bbb][process_end_ok] 0.000s      ✗ noise
LOG-15

Details are terse, on one line. details are human-readable and terse, and never contain a physical newline.

logs.md
LOG-16

No secrets or payloads in details. details never contain secrets, tokens, signed URLs, URL query values, bodies or headers. Prefer a reference to the payload over the payload.

logs.md
LOG-17

Simple words bare, the rest JSON-quoted. A printable ASCII word without spaces, double quotes, backslashes or square brackets is written bare — exactly the bytes that were sent, so it cannot span words, break the line, or mint a fake tag. Every other string is JSON-quoted.

logs.md
name=select_users
reason="db timeout"
value=""
LOG-18

Structures as compact JSON. Arrays, objects, booleans and null use compact JSON.

logs.md
retry=true limits={"soft":10,"hard":25}
LOG-19

An unordered list is sorted and prefixed with its count. Ordered values are not sorted.

logs.md
3:[180,783,846]
2:["bar","foo"]
0:[]
LOG-20

Truncate on UTF-8, count what is cut. Truncation preserves valid UTF-8 and ends with the number of omitted bytes.

logs.md
...+4821
LOG-21

Keep one log line under 2k UTF-8 bytes. A log line describes an event; it is not payload storage.

logs.md
LOG-22

group_exit is optional; nothing follows it. group_exit is optional and mainly serves to detect leaks. After it is emitted, no producer emits another event for that group; a parent may emit it for work it abandons. Consumers must accept groups without it — its absence makes no claim.

logs.md
[group_uid][group_exit]
LOG-23

After means emission order, not timestamps. “After” group_exit means producer emission order, not timestamp or collector ingestion order. Buffering may deliver an older event later; that alone is not an error. Without a causal-order signal — preserved per-group order, a shared sequence — cross-process detection is advisory.

logs.md

CSSClasses and stylesA fixed class order; every class has a rule.

CSS-01

Utilities first, app classes next, local classes last. Classes inside one class="…" attribute keep a fixed order. Plain utilities lead; an app-prefixed class (vb-*, np-* — one prefix per app, app-* in these examples) sorts after all of them, base class included; a file-local #-* class is always last.

css_classes.md
layout  spacing  sizing  decoration  typography  app-prefix  local

<div class="flex-row-c #-root" />
<div class="fluid p30 xpt app-scrollbars-light #-grid" />
<div class="db w80 h80 br4 fit-cover cur-pointer app-background #-preset-img" />
<div class="flex-row-cl gap10 app-font-b14 #-title-trigger" />
CSS-02

Item class leads; gap closes the layout. Within the utilities: an item class (fluid, grow, shrink, flex-fluid, flex-grow, flex-nogrow, flex-shrink, flex-noshrink, flex-static) or a display or position utility (db, abs) leads where the element carries one; a gap* closes the layout group — every flex*, grid* or split class first, then the gap; grid* and flex* never share an element; ph* precedes pv*, and spacing comes before typography.

css_classes.md
fluid flex-row gap10 oa
flex-row flex-align-center gap10 mt10
flex-col-c gap15
grid-foo gap5
CSS-03

No class without a rule. Every class either has a rule in the file’s own style block or is an established project utility. An element that needs no styling stays classless — a label-only class rots and sends the next reader looking for a rule nobody wrote.

css_classes.md
<!-- the wrapper is not styled, so it carries no class -->
<div>
    <div class="#-funnel-bars">...</div>
</div>
CSS-04

Gap for flex and grid, mg and mi for blocks. gap* spaces the children of a grid or flex container; mg* and mi* are the block-container forms. The two do not mix.

css_classes.md
CSS-05

Fluid in a split, flex-fluid in a flex. fluid marks the filling child of an hsplit/vsplit (whose children default to flex: none); flex-fluid marks the growing child of a plain flex-row/flex-col. Same CSS — the choice states which container the element sits in.

css_classes.md
CSS-06

The x class comes before its setter. An x* class usually comes before the setter it clears the way for — the broad class leads and the narrow one corrects it, whichever of the two is the reset.

css_classes.md
<div class="xm ml5" />   <!-- margin: 0; margin-left: 5px; -->
<div class="m5 xml" />   <!-- margin: 5px; margin-left: 0;  -->
CSS-07

Rows and columns are a table. Rows and columns are a <table>, not a stack of flex rows — the columns line up only until one cell is wider. Flex rows stay for content that is genuinely not tabular.

css_classes.md
CSS-08

Imports and includes come first. @import comes first in a block; @include comes first in a rule, ahead of the property declarations — the mixin brings the base, the block overrides it.

css_classes.md
.#-card
    @include app-transition(box-shadow, border-color)
    box-sizing: border-box
CSS-09

Transitions come from the mixin. A transition: property is not written by hand — @include app-transition(props…) fills it, expanding each property into <prop> <speed> against the one shared speed. app-transition-fast and app-transition-debug are the same mixin at the fast and debug speeds. List the exact properties that change, never all, and put the include on the base rule rather than the state variant, so the animation covers both directions.

css_classes.md
@include app-transition(box-shadow, border-color)
CSS-10

Five families: layout, spacing, sizing, decoration, typography. What each family holds: layout is the flex/grid/split container and its flex-* modifiers; spacing is p* / m*; sizing is w* / h* / max-w* / min-h*; decoration is br*, fit-cover, cur-pointer and the other shape and surface utilities; typography is fs* fw* lh*, then alignment and nowrap.

css_classes.md
CSS-11

A header aligns like its column. A table header is aligned the way its column's data is: centered data, centered header; right-aligned data, right-aligned header.

css_classes.md
CSS-12

One selector per line. A selector list puts each selector on its own line, the comma closing the line; the brace follows the last one.

css_classes.md
.docs th, .docs td {   ✗ no

.docs th,
.docs td {             ✓ yes
CSS-13

One blank line between rules. Rules stand one blank line apart: each closing brace is followed by one empty line before the next selector — never two, never none.

css_classes.md
.hidden {
    display: none !important;
}
.intro {          ✗ no blank line

.hidden {
    display: none !important;
}

.intro {          ✓ one blank line

SQLSQL queriesMySQL: upper-case keywords; the query laid out like code.

SQL-01

A long query opens and closes on its own line. A query that spans lines opens its template literal with a line break and closes it on a line of its own; the query is indented one level deeper than the call that runs it.

sql.md
await knex.raw(`
    UPDATE
        user_identities
    ...
`);
SQL-02

Keywords upper case, names lower case. Every keyword, type and function is upper case; tables, columns, indexes and aliases stay lower case, spelled as the schema spells them.

sql.md
SELECT MIN(id) AS id FROM user_identities   ✓ yes
select min(id) as id from user_identities   ✗ no
SQL-03

Each clause on its own line. The dialect is MySQL. At the top level of a statement, each clause starts a line of its own — SELECT, FROM, every JOIN, UPDATE, SET, CREATE UNIQUE INDEX, ON, WHERE, ALTER TABLE, DROP INDEX — and what the clause takes goes on the next line, indented four spaces. A keyword of several words stays on one line.

sql.md
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX
    user_identities_primary_user_id_unique
ON
    user_identities (primary_user_id)

DROP INDEX
    user_identities_primary_user_id_unique
ON
    user_identities
SQL-04

A subquery body is indented between its parentheses. A subquery opens with ( at the end of the line that uses it; its body is indented one level, and ) closes it on a line of its own at that line's indent, followed by the alias.

sql.md
WHERE id IN (
    SELECT id FROM (
        SELECT MIN(id) AS id
        ...
    ) AS oldest
)
SQL-05

Short expressions stay on one line. A short expression stays on one line: a WHERE that opens a subquery, even at the top level, and the clauses inside a subquery.

sql.md
WHERE id IN (
    SELECT id FROM (
        SELECT MIN(id) AS id
        FROM user_identities
SQL-06

One ALTER TABLE action per clause. Each action of an ALTER TABLE is a clause of its own, its operand indented under it; the comma between two actions ends the first operand's line. A column definition stays whole on its line.

sql.md
ALTER TABLE
    user_identities
DROP INDEX
    user_identities_primary_user_id_unique,
DROP COLUMN
    primary_user_id

VUEVue 2Components that behave like the platform.

VUE-01

Every component is provided with three global methods through a mixin.

vue-globals.md
px(value)        // format a pixel value
uid([name])      // ids unique across components
emit_input(value) // return a value from an input
VUE-02

Ids come from uid. Generated ids are bound to the current element and are what id and label[for] use. The name uid was chosen so it does not conflict with the id attribute every element may carry.

vue-globals.md
uid: function (name) {
    return name ? `c${this._uid}_${name}` : `c${this._uid}`;
},
VUE-03

Spell out v-on and v-bind. The shorthands @ and : are not used.

vue-formatting.md
<img v-bind:src="photo.thumbnail_url" v-bind:alt="photo.title" />
VUE-04

Attributes keep one order.

vue-formatting.md
ref v-if v-for v-on v-bind:ref v-bind [...] class type placeholder title
VUE-05

Lift v-if off a v-for. Avoid v-if and v-for on the same component — lift the condition to a <template>.

vue-formatting.md
<template v-if="items">
    <div v-for="item in items" v-bind:key="item.uid">
        {{ item.title }}
    </div>
</template>
VUE-06

Compound directive values in parentheses. A simple directive value stays bare; a compound one is wrapped in parentheses. Every directive — v-if, v-else-if, v-show, v-on, v-bind. Simple is a single identifier, member access, method call, template literal or unary negation; compound is anything carrying a binary operator or a ternary.

vue-formatting.md
<template v-if="is_ready">
<template v-if="(is_loading_fonts || is_loading_images)">
<div v-bind:class="(compact ? 'narrow' : 'wide')" />
VUE-07

An input works like a native input. Anything which takes data from a user is called an input and must work as a normal INPUT element.

vue-input.md
  1. takes data from the value property
  2. emits an input event
  3. respects the disabled state
  4. respects the readonly attribute
  5. reacts to clicks on the associated LABEL
  6. reacts to mouse hover from that LABEL
  7. injects and uses app_form_input_id
  8. takes focus with the TAB key
VUE-08

Avoid generic inputs. Avoid generic inputs — those with a lot of properties like min, max, step.

vue-input.md
VUE-09

Forms submit by button and Enter. Compose forms from app-form-div and app-label, inside a <form> whose submit the submit button and the Enter key both reach.

vue-form.md
<form v-on:submit.prevent="submit" class="mg10">
    <app-form-div class="flex-row gap10">
        <app-label>Email:</app-label>
        <app-input-email v-model="user.email" />
    </app-form-div>
</form>
VUE-10

Cancel and submit close the form. A form’s buttons close the form: cancel returns false through vue-modal’s modal.return, submit is a type="submit" button.

vue-form.md
<app-button-orange v-on:click="modal.return(false)">
    Cancel
</app-button-orange>
<app-button-green type="submit">
    Submit
</app-button-green>
VUE-11

One button, one class.

vue-button.md
VUE-12

A slider thumb moves from 0 to 100%. A slider is a container and a thumb. Position the thumb with top or left from 0 to 100% — 0 means empty, 100% means full.

vue-slider.md
left: 0      // empty
left: 100%   // full
VUE-13

One SVG icon per file. Each SVG icon goes into its own svg-icon-*.vue file, containing only a TEMPLATE element with an SVG inside.

vue-svg-icon.md
<template>
    <svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
        <path fill="currentColor" d="..." />
    </svg>
</template>
VUE-14

Icons use currentColor. SVG icons respect the currentColor CSS property.

vue-svg-icon.md
<path fill="currentColor" d="..." />
VUE-15

Component options keep one order.

vue-components.md
props inject provide mixins data computed watch methods mounted created beforeDestroy
VUE-16

Name a handler by event and button text. An event handler is named after the UI part it is bound to — the event, then the button text.

vue-components.md
<button v-on:click="click_approve">
    Approve
</button>
VUE-17

A handler on an icon is named after the icon.

vue-components.md
<button v-on:click="click_icon_archive">
    <svg-icon-archive />
</button>
VUE-18

Rename the handler with its label. After the text or icon is changed, rename the corresponding event handler.

vue-components.md
Approve → Accept     // click_approve → click_accept
VUE-19

Empty elements close themselves. An element without a body closes itself — a component, an HTML element and a void element alike. This holds in .vue files and string templates; an in-DOM template is parsed by the browser first.

vue-formatting.md
<th></th>   ✗ no
<th />       ✓ yes

<app-input-email v-model="user.email" />
VUE-20

A piece shown in two places is a component. Whatever the screen shows in more than one place, a badge most often, is a Vue component of its own, used in each place. Never the same markup and classes copied: a change then reaches some copies and misses the others.

vue-components.md
<span class="flex-row-cl gap5 br999 #-reply">   ✗ no
    In progress {{ detail }}
</span>

<badge-in-progress v-bind:detail="detail" />   ✓ yes
VUE-21

Named kind first. A component is named <kind>-<what it says>, as icons are svg-icon-*. Sorted by name, every component of a kind sits together.

vue-components.md
badge-filing
badge-in-progress
badge-no-reply
VUE-22

What changes is a prop. What differs from place to place goes in as a prop: a count, a time, a plan's progress. The component holds the rest.

vue-components.md
<badge-new v-bind:count="3" />              // 3 new
<badge-in-progress detail="for 4 h" />
VUE-23

A variant is a suffix. A smaller or otherwise different form is a component of its own, named with a suffix; never a second copy written by hand where it is needed.

vue-components.md
badge-in-progress → badge-in-progress-sm
VUE-24

A kind shares one look through one mixin. What every component of a kind shares, its shape, size and type, comes from one Sass mixin; each component sets only its own colours.

vue-components.md
.#-root
    @include app-badge
    background: var(--accent-soft)
    color: var(--accent)

UIUI appearanceHow a screen looks.

UI-01

Every screen has a light/dark switch. An app screen, a report, a standalone page: each shows a switch the reader can click. Following the OS setting alone does not count. One exception: a page made only to be photographed for a rule's picture keeps no switch.

theme_switch.md
UI-02

Two states, one shared icon button. Show the current theme: sun for Light, crescent for Dark. Use img/theme-sun.svg and img/theme-moon.svg; size and border may vary. Click toggles directly, with no menu, System or Auto option.

theme_switch.md
Sun: Light → Crescent: Dark → Sun: Light
UI-03

The dark theme redefines the light colors. The light colors live on :root; the dark theme sets the same variables under :root[data-theme="dark"].

theme_switch.md
:root {
    --color-bg: #FFFFFF;
    --color-text: #1B1F23;
}
:root[data-theme="dark"] {
    --color-bg: #15181C;
    --color-text: #E6E8EB;
}
UI-04

The theme is set before the page shows. The page reads the saved choice from localStorage (the OS setting once, when nothing is saved), puts it on <html> as data-theme, and saves each new choice; storage access sits in try/catch.

theme_switch.md
document.documentElement.dataset.theme = theme;
UI-05

The switch stays in reach on a long page. When the header scrolls away, a copy of the switch appears at the right end of the sticky bar.

theme_switch.md
UI-06

Every project page opens with the same header. The project on the left; GitHub and the theme switch on the right; search and section links between them, the search lined up with the content column.

page_header.md
UI-07

Left: icon, name, version. The project's icon when it has one, its name, and its released version.

page_header.md
[icon]  Authwall Docs  v1.16.0
UI-08

Right: the links, then the theme switch, always last. The GitHub icon links to the repository; other links, such as Twitter or Facebook, sit beside it. However many links a project has, the switch stays at the right edge, the same on every page. The icons look alike: one size, no frame on any of them.

page_header.md
[GitHub]  [Twitter]  [Current theme icon]

UIMUI mechanicsHow a screen works.

UIM-01

Nothing jumps. In a list or a grid, the item the reader works with, the one selected or being looked at, stays where it is on the screen while the app adds, removes or grows items above, below or beside it — a new message, a summary that finishes loading; the scroll position adjusts instead, as far as the list's ends allow. A control that docks or hides as the page scrolls is outside this rule.

scroll_anchoring.md
UIM-02

Keep the place yourself; the browser won't. Before such a change, note the element in the middle of the view and where it is on the screen; after the change, scroll by however far it moved. The browser keeps the place only when the change is entirely above the view: not at the very top, not when the growing block is itself on screen, not after a re-render.

scroll_anchoring.md
const keep = scroll_keep(scroller);
await keep(async function () {
    summary.text = text;
    await vm.$nextTick();
});
UIM-03

Test it. For each kind of change, a test notes where the middle element is, makes the change, and checks it moved 0 px — at the top of the view and in the middle. One more check runs without the fix and must see the jump.

scroll_anchoring.md
assert.equal(shift, 0);
UIM-04

A file input also takes a drop. Anything that lets the user pick files also takes files dragged onto it; anything that lets them pick a whole folder also takes a folder dragged onto it.

file_drop.md
UIM-05

The drop takes what the dialog takes. The same file types, one or many; a whole folder when the dialog picks folders, read file by file. A dropped file goes down the same path as a picked one.

file_drop.md
file_drop_bind(element, input, take);

// the input says what the dialog takes
if (entry.isFile || input.webkitdirectory)
take(files_as_dialog_takes(files, input));
UIM-06

Show the drop target; never lose the page. The element lights up while files are dragged over it, and a file dropped beside it does not open in the tab.

file_drop.md
window.addEventListener('dragover', v => v.preventDefault());
window.addEventListener('drop', v => v.preventDefault());
UIM-07

Trust the user: no "Are you sure?". Delete, rename, move, cancel: it happens at once, and the user keeps working.

no_confirmations.md
UIM-08

Undo instead. A deleted thing goes to a trash; a rename, an edit or a move can be undone. The way back is right there after the action.

no_confirmations.md
Deleted · Undo
UIM-09

Confirm only what cannot be undone and costs a lot. Closing an account, erasing data for good. Even then, not an OK/Cancel box but a deliberate step: typing the name, or a link sent by email.

no_confirmations.md
UIM-10

Use optimistic updates; the user keeps working. Keep the backend snapshot immutable and local pending changes separate. Show the local change and send its update immediately. After acknowledgement, reread the backend, replace the snapshot, and clear only the pending change confirmed by that result; preserve later actions and reject stale refreshes. Show the change where the user made it, at once, marked as waiting, whatever route it takes inside. Keep failures visible as unsynchronized and retry safely; if only the reread failed, retry that step.

optimistic_updates.md
Read → local overlay → update → acknowledgement
→ refresh → replace snapshot → clear confirmed overlay
UIM-11

Typing focuses the main search, first character included. On a page with one primary search/filter, typing outside editable fields focuses it immediately and enters the first character too. Local inputs retain their typing; respect shortcuts and native keyboard behavior.

main_search.md
Click background → type sm → main filter contains sm
UIM-12

Select the first actionable item by default. In a list of action targets, the first visible actionable item in displayed order is selected by default; Enter acts on it. An explicit user selection wins. A new filtered list defaults to its first actionable item; an empty list has no action.

default_list_item.md
SQLite, LinkedIn → Enter opens SQLite
UIM-13

Show only what works. A control the app already knows will fail is not drawn as if it would work: an expired option, the button of an ended chat, an action the user has no right to. Nobody presses a button to be told "Sorry, this has expired".

dead_controls.md
UIM-14

Ask the action first: a dry run. Every action can answer "would it work now?" without doing anything. The screen asks before drawing the control, and again whenever the answer can change; a button that expires on screen changes at that moment, not on the next click.

dead_controls.md
can_end_chat(chat) → false
→ no End chat button
UIM-15

No means hidden, or disabled with the reason on it. Hide what nobody would look for there; disable what the user expects in its place, with the reason written on it or beside it. Never a control whose only answer comes after the click.

dead_controls.md
Expired yesterday at 10:51

DOCWriting the rulesHow a document in this repo is built.

DOC-01

A document has two halves. The author writes the top half, compressed around what he already knows; the AI writes the bottom half, restating it for a reader who lacks that context.

WRITING.md
DOC-02

Author sources govern the explanation. Read the top half and applicable manually approved rules. An approved entry may explicitly clarify older wording within its scope; if the sources disagree without such a decision, ask before regenerating.

WRITING.md
DOC-03

No AI patches the top half. The one exception is an explicit request from the author.

WRITING.md
DOC-04

Regenerate the bottom half from both sources, never edit it. After the top half or an applicable manually approved rule changes, regenerate the explanation from both. Preserve approved decisions and their scope.

WRITING.md
DOC-05

Usually a heading starts the bottom half. Most of the time the bottom half starts with a # heading, and that heading is the boundary. A --- line or a closing fence before it is decoration. There is no strict marker.

WRITING.md
--- ✨ AI-Generated Content Below ✨ ---
DOC-06

One audit, one file; its register is the issue list. The report of a full audit is one file, notes/audit-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md. The projects have no issue tracker: the finding register of the newest audit note is the issue list, and later audits refer to findings by their ids.

audit_note.md
notes/audit-2026-09-02.md
DOC-07

Audit notes keep one section order. An audit note keeps one order: title, repository line, scope, verdict with a health-at-a-glance table, finding register, findings, what is good, recommended order of work, status of prior findings, file inventory.

audit_note.md
DOC-08

Scope says what ran and what did not. The scope lists every check actually run, and what was not exercised. A check which was not run is said so; it is never implied.

audit_note.md
DOC-09

Findings have permanent ids and evidence. A finding id is <PROJECT>-NN, never reused and never renumbered. Each finding is one section citing file:line and the evidence — the quoted lines, the command which was run and what it printed.

audit_note.md
### DEMO-01 Classes banned in one file, shown in another (high)
DOC-10

Audit notes have no top half and stay untracked. An audit note is written by the AI as a whole, so it has no top half and no separator. It is left untracked; it is committed only on request.

audit_note.md
DOC-11

Keep manually approved rules outside regenerated text. Record only explicit author decisions in MANUALLY_APPROVED_RULES.md, with scope, approval date and evidence. Read applicable entries when rewriting explanations. Maintain the approval file; never regenerate it or treat an AI suggestion as approval.

MANUALLY_APPROVED_RULES.md
author source + manually approved rules
→ regenerated explanation
DOC-12

A document without an author section is open to requested edits. A document with no author notes above a heading is an ordinary file: the AI edits it for the task asked. Where the author's section exists, it stays on top and is never overwritten. When its end is unclear, ask first.

WRITING.md
author notes        → never overwritten
# Heading
explanation         → regenerated

no author notes     → edited on request
DOC-13

A glossary keeps the author's terms; the AI explains below them. Everything before the first ## section (title, note, groups, term list) is the author's and is never rewritten. Each ## section explains one term and is regenerated from the author's line.

WRITING.md
# Testing (TEST)           yours
- Flaky Test – …           yours

## Intermittent failures   AI
DOC-14

A GIF shows its time and its progress. Every GIF in the docs is recorded at 30 frames a second, counts its time from 0 at its first frame in a corner, and has a thin bar along its top that fills as it plays; both start again when it loops.

gifs.md

LINTStated by the linterRules that only LINTING.md and the preset spell out.

LINT-01

Spaces around operators, except multiplicative ones. Multiplicative operators are tight — *, /, **. Every other binary, logical and assignment operator has a space on each side.

LINTING.md
const x = a*b + c/d - e**2;
const x = a % 2;
LINT-02

Space before an anonymous function's parenthesis. An anonymous function has a space before its parenthesis; a named one has none.

LINTING.md
server.on('error', function (error) {
});

function main()
{
}
LINT-03

Tiny arrows fit one line. A tiny arrow is a single-line expression callback or value factory, passed as a call argument or as an object property value; an empty () => {} is one too (FMT-32). Options-style methods retain function expressions (FMT-12); literal methods: {...} tables reject arrows. It fits one line; the number of parameters does not matter. A lone value/event parameter is v, nested vv by total arrow depth; an error parameter stays e at every depth (VAR-05), including .catch, .then rejection callbacks and EventEmitter error listeners. It is taken whole — v => v.uid, not ({uid}) => uid. A named helper is a function declaration.

LINTING.md
LINT-04

Use for...of, not forEach. forEach does not exist. Use for...of.

LINTING.md
items.forEach(function (item) {   ✗ no
});

for (const item of items) {       ✓ yes
}
LINT-06

Imports first: side effects, defaults, named. Imports are the first statements of a file, one statement per line, in up to three blocks: side-effect imports — import './x', a bare require('x') — first, in the order they run; then the sorted default imports; then, if set apart, the sorted named imports ({foo, bar}). One blank line may separate the blocks.

LINTING.md
LINT-07

The project picks its module format. Module format is the consuming project’s choice: JavaScript defaults to ES modules, .cjs is CommonJS, and the sorting rule supports both import forms. CommonJS-only is this repository’s own rule.

LINTING.md
LINT-08

A layout and its gap share a class value. gap* closes the layout group: the flex/grid/split container, then its flex-* modifiers, then the gap. Put a layout and its gap in the same class value.

LINTING.md
LINT-09

Font size and weight before line height. Within typography, fs* and fw* come before lh*. Several local #-* classes together form the final group.

LINTING.md
LINT-10

Write #- only where the loader replaces it. #- is written only in the forms the hashtag loader replaces: a double-quoted class, card_class or attribute ending in -class / :class; .#- in a style block; and the exact single-quoted '.#- form in JavaScript.

LINTING.md
LINT-11

Every #- class has a real style. Each statically known #-* class has a nonempty style selector in the same component. Declarations, includes and extends count as styles; an empty rule, a variable-only rule, or a mention inside :not(...) does not.

LINTING.md
LINT-12

A Vue script indents four spaces. A Vue <script> is indented four spaces with one base indent.

LINTING.md

No rule matches that.

In the canonical forms, ✓ and ✗ are verdicts, not code. The same index as a plain table: rules.md The words: The Glossaries github.com/vbarbarosh/rules
